To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maintenance regimen of bevacizumbab in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic teleangectasia should be monthly infusions of 5 mg/Kg.
the relationship between the serum concentration of bevacizumb and both the cardiac index and epistasis duration in patients with hereditary hemorrhagic teangiectasia was investigated.
the maintenance dose of bevacizumbab in HHT patients was determined to be 5 mg/kg monthly, to control both cardiac index and frequency of epistaxis.

the development of a pharmacokinetic-phamacodynamic model of the effects of bevacizunab in hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasie patients with severe liver shunts.
the design of the maintenance dose of bevacizunab in patients suffering from HHT and high-output cardiac failure.
the dose - response relationship of a novel drug in a rare genetic disease.

bevacizumabbased therapy is a promising therapeutic option for HHT patients with cardiac failure and/or refractory epistaxis, and that monthly maintenance infusions of 5 mg kg-1 should be considered.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maintenance dosing regimen with 5 mg/kg of bevacizamab every month should be the best option to treat HHT patients with high cardiac index.

the dose-response relationship of bevacuzimab in patients with HHT is not well defined.
